rationale: The target requires braking behaviour itself to be characterised, so including vehicle braking and stopping is not an extraneous control-response expansion. H-3 establishes sudden stopping without an obstacle as the hazardous event, while SG-3 and FR-7 support distinguishing unintended braking from braking justified by an obstacle. P retains the stated operational context without incorporating sensing, computation, failure mitigation, communication, or mechanism-specific timing.
determining_elements: “Vehicle braking behavior” and whether the vehicle “brakes or stops unexpectedly” directly address prevention of unintended braking.
The relationship between braking and the presence or absence of an actual obstacle requiring braking is supported by H-3 and FR-7 and characterises whether braking is justified.
The declared straight-ahead, 50 km/h, good-weather urban-road context with no visible obstacles or vehicles in front matches H-3's operational situation.
